about: The hero types of layout v4 (references/layout-v4.md section 3), each built in this folder as hero-<id>.html and shot at 1440x900, 1024x768, 820x1180 and 390x844. A builder deals one at random by the brief's type and the material it really has: node <skill>/assets/layout/deal.mjs --type <software|product|service> --has <photo,ui,film,object,ground>. A place's hero is never dealt: it is always 'place' (local-business Recipe 3, hero-place.html), and no other hero lists place. Every hero is exactly one screen (height 100svh) with the fixed header (72px, 56 on a phone) over its top: its words start 48px under the header (y 120 at 1440x900, y 96 at 390x844; 40 and 24 under a place's photograph), its content ends 64px above the fold (24 on a phone, plus the action bar), and nothing of the next section shows. Its blocks stand on the container's two lines (x 80 and 1360 at 1440, 24 and 366 at 390) or run edge to edge; never out to one viewport edge only. Nothing is laid over a photograph to make words readable (no scrim, gradient or veil: PH-31). Numbers are px, measured on the demos (check.mjs prints them): [1440x900, 390x844]. h1 sizes in 'size' are before --ly-scale; the measured ones in at1440/at390 are after the demo's scale.

fields.types: business types it may be dealt to, with weights; a type missing is never dealt. place is never dealt: deal.mjs always prints the 'place' hero for it. gaming is a kind, not a page type (a game is page type software): its weights are read by deal.mjs for a game (--kind gaming, or --type software --has film,photo without ui) and never for a software brief; no hero for a game lists ui. A game without art files passes --has setting (stand-in photographs of its setting, found with photos.mjs search) and is printed the photo hero, its name set large on the photograph's calm side; --has object (its key art rendered with assets/objects/product-render) only when the brief asks for 3D. A game never deals statement or word: an effect never replaces its key art
fields.needs: the material it cannot do without (a|b means either): photo (a strong photograph of the real thing, at least 1920 wide for a full-bleed one: the client's own, else a stand-in found with photos.mjs search and listed in the report), ui (the client's screens or kit fragments from assets/ui rewritten to its names), film (a real film; without one the control links to the film's page, never a dead button), object (a product photograph on a plain ground, a cut-out, the client's render, or a product render composed with assets/objects/product-render when the brief asks for 3D or a render), setting (a game without art files: stand-in photographs of the place its world is set in), ground (nothing: a CSS ground from assets/backgrounds)
fields.h1: the layout.css token, its size at 1440 and 390 before --ly-scale, the leading, the most lines at each width and the longest headline that fits
fields.grid: where each block stands on the 12 columns at 1440 (from 1024 up); below 1024 everything stacks in the order given
fields.at1440: measured on the demo at 1440x900 (the fixed header 72 over the hero's top, the hero exactly 900, words from y 120, content ending by y 836, container x 80 to 1360)
fields.at390: measured on the demo at 390x844 (header 56, the hero exactly 844, words from y 96, content ending by y 820, container x 24 to 366)
fields.moment: the hero's own small motion (layout.js) after the entrance every hero makes once on load (data-enter, motion.md), how it rests, and what reduced motion and a phone show; 'none' means nothing more than that entrance. The page's dealt moments are apart (moments.mjs pick). On kind other (site-kind other) and on a place nothing moves by itself: the live word, the collage sets and the steps rest on their first or finished picture (pointer-driven letters and hover stay)
fields.moments: assets/moments/index.json ids that may be dealt onto this hero (one at most; moments.mjs pick --fits hero decides), as { id, only? }: only "tech" means software, AI and gaming briefs only
fields.grounds: assets/backgrounds/index.json ids the hero may stand on, as { id, only?, dark? }: only "tech" for software, AI and gaming briefs only; dark true for a dark page only
fields.effects: assets/effects ids the hero's visual may carry, as { id, as? }: every effect is for tech, software, AI and gaming briefs only, never a place or a local business; 'as' says where it goes when that is not the visual itself
fields.mistakes: what makes it fail the house's look
fields.avoid: the material that rules it out: with it in --has the hero is never dealt (word and statement are for briefs without a strong photograph or a film; with one, it leads)

heroes.name: Product stage with one object
heroes.from: Figma's hero row, Apple product pages, Cowboy, Teenage Engineering
heroes.job: The product itself, big, under one head row: the headline left, the lead and the buttons right. A render or a cut-out stands on the page's own ground across the wrap (no box, no gradient, no radius), its widest view (a bike's side) spanning 80% or more of the wrap at 1440; a product photograph runs edge to edge down to the fold, cropped so the product spans 80% or more of the wrap. Nothing on the product: no hotspots by default (the parts are named in the sections below). A product or hardware without photographs of its own: a stand-in photograph of the same kind of thing (photos.mjs search), listed in the report; its product render (assets/objects/product-render), a still, only when the brief asks for 3D or a render. A game puts its name in the h1 (or its wordmark above it), the launch date or status in the lead, and the stage holds its key art (a rendered hero object or world only when the brief asks for 3D; a print or scene keeps the lit stage), an effect allowed only behind it.
